Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions. Fixed-law bigram exception (q_7dbb0e and new controlled panel): GRU64x2 AdamW .003, beta2=.95, wd=.001, batch32 wins6/6 genuinely weak transformer pairs atT256 but loses5/6 atT1024 across three fixed800-window datasets. lr*T=3.072 does not imply progress or measured parameter motion.
